title: Microburst
tagline: A thunderstorm sits on the final approach at Gatwick.
history: Inspired by approaches flown into thunderstorm downbursts — a 1985 accident above all — that led to airborne windshear detection and the escape manoeuvre every airline pilot now practises.
situation: Seven miles out on the ILS for Gatwick's 26L in the late afternoon, a storm cell is drifting across the final approach. First the speed will rise in a headwind — then the air falls out from under you.
failures: Microburst on the final approach: headwind gain, 2,000+ ft/min downdraft, then tailwind
tips: At the WINDSHEAR warning: TOGA thrust at once, pitch towards 15°, wings level
Do not change the configuration (gear, flaps) until clear
Ride the stall warning if you must — never let the speed decay further

do.note: ATC: Go-around noted — climb straight ahead to 3,000 ft.

objectives.text: Escape: climb back through 1,500 ft above the ground
